cf-2-144.title: The Repaired Valve
cf-2-144.text: Perseverance pays against the stubborn friction of rusted metal, leaving the float-valve seated true and firm within its housing. Hot water ceases its wasteful hiss, settling into a steady, pressurized hum that steadies the boiler gauge. A handful of heavy copper washers and a stout tin of yellow anti-friction grease are your reward for the trouble, tucked safely into the tool-chest before you step back onto the footplate.

cf-2-145.title: Beneath the Iron Tank
cf-2-145.text: Thick crusts of grey alkali flake away beneath your scraper as you clear the choked drainage pipe beneath the roadside water tank. Stagnant moisture breaks free at last with a foul, heavy gurgle, spilling into the dry ballast below and clearing the drain-hole at long last. Probing the recess reveals a stout, oil-stained tool wedged in the mud, which proves upon inspection to be a rusted but serviceable brass grease-gun.

cf-2-146.title: The Clogged Drain
cf-2-146.text: Sludge and cinders have packed the overflow channel beneath the massive tender until it resembles hard cement. Working the bent iron poker back and forth loosens the plug of debris, letting foul water drain away from the axle-boxes where it might otherwise cause dangerous rot. The cleared pipe breathes out a damp, mineral smell of sulfur and cold earth into the dry wind.

cf-2-147.title: Clearing the Blocked Pipe
cf-2-147.text: Stubborn corrosion locks the lower drain-cock tight, threatening to twist the copper feed-line right off its mounting brackets if you apply too much force. You brace your boot against the iron chassis plate, grip the heavy pipe-wrench with both hands, and lean all your weight into a slow, measured torque while the ancient metal groans beneath the strain.

cf-2-148.title: The Snapped Feed-Line
cf-2-148.text: The seized brass fitting shears clean off with a sharp crack, spraying a jet of scalding, greasy water across your sleeve and scalding your wrist before you can wrench the shut-off valve closed. Precious steam pressure bleeds away into the alkali dust, and you are left binding the weeping joint with soaked hemp cord and cursing the unforgiving metal.

cf-2-149.title: The Grease-Gun
cf-2-149.text:
Thick rust flakes fall from the drainpipe into your palm as the choked channel finally spits its foul sediment into the ash-dune below. The pressure gauge on the side of the boiler settles into a steadier rhythm, sighing with relief as the trapped water finds its proper course. Among the grit and discarded scrap beneath the valve housing, your fingers close around a heavy iron cylinder wrapped in greasy rag. It is a battered but serviceable brass grease-gun, its leather plunger still supple enough to force lubricant into stubborn journal-boxes when the mileage mounts.

Wiping the nozzle on your trouser leg, you secure the tool in the cab locker alongside the spare oil can.

cf-2-150.title: Midnight on the Steppe
cf-2-150.text:
The storm clock hanging above the fire-door clicks its heavy iron tooth toward midnight, shaking loose a fine drift of grey soot across the brass dial. Far across the grey flats, from the direction of the towering viaduct, a deep metallic groaning rolls through the ground like the turning of a subterranean engine. The horizon shivers under a low bank of bruised purple clouds where the ash-storm season gathers its strength.

You check the water glass one more time, feeling the steady thrum of the copper boiler against your palms as the Marrowbone waits for the signal to move.

cf-2-151.title: The Iron Scriptorium
cf-2-151.text: A derelict telegraph carriage sits abandoned beside the tracks, its windows frosted with alkali and salt, yet a single yellow lamp still burns behind the warped wooden door. Inside, a lone clerk in a frayed uniform records the passage of phantom trains in a ledger that never ends, surrounded by ticking sounders and mountains of damp paper. The place smells of stale tobacco and ozone, offering shelter from the rising wind and multiple paths deeper into the ash-steppeland.

cf-2-152.title: The Flickering Sounder
cf-2-152.text: Brass arms twitch erratically across the glass-covered dial as the telegraph key chatters out a rapid, fractured sequence of dots and dashes. By watching the rhythm of the stuttering needle, you piece together a warning meant for the patrol posts up-line about railhead blockades and armed patrols moving out from the viaduct. The knowledge rests heavy in your mind as the paper ribbon falls silent.

cf-2-153.title: The Flickering Needle
cf-2-153.text: Glass tremors in the brass frame as the telegraph relay chatters out a frantic staccato against the wooden wall of the waystation. The paper tape uncoils in a jerky dance, punching neat holes that spell out the movements of the armored patrol cars stationed three miles up the line. Every strike of the armature sounds like a dry knuckle rapping on a coffin lid, marking the precise hours the Barons intend to lock the junction switches. You commit the sequence of dots and dashes to memory, watching the ink fade into the cheap pulp paper as the needle finally falls still.
exits: Pocket the decoded slip and run

cf-2-154.title: Decoding the Wire
cf-2-154.text: The paper ribbon feeds through the embossing machine too fast, smudging the ink dots into an unintelligible blur of Morse code while the signal needle chatters frantically against its brass stop. You squint through the dim lamplight, trying to isolate the code-groups for military patrols from the random static of the atmospheric storm before the needle drops dead.

cf-2-155.title: The Static Blur
cf-2-155.text: Static discharge leaps from the brass sounder with a sharp snap, charring the paper tape to black ash and leaving your ears ringing with a high, thin whine. You stumble back against the shelving, scattering a dozen outdated waybills across the floorboards and losing precious minutes to the confusion before you can steady your breathing.

cf-2-156.title: The Scriptorium Ink
cf-2-156.text: Blue ink dries slowly on the damp parchment of the ledger while the telegraph key chatters its warning from across the deserted carriage. You trace the freshly stamped route manifest with a soot-stained thumb, noting the specific hours the armored patrol carriages clear the lower embankment. The clerk has already packed his inkwells into a leather satchel, leaving behind only the carbon copy of the dispatch and a silent nod of complicity. It is a precarious edge to walk, but knowing which switch-lever the Barons plan to drop next gives you a narrow channel through the grey waste.
exits: Step back out to the platform
